title: Planning maps each goal clause to a check that reads every part of it, its isolation parts included
goal: kb/_self/backlog.md's sprint Plan rules and the kb-sprint skill's plan step say that a check mapped to a goal clause reads every part of that clause (each named class, row, arm, and an isolation part such as a scratch home or no forge call), and that a part no check reads is split into its own clause with its own check before the start gate; the rule is a tested question of the kb-sprint:plan set

run:
import sys
def _fail(t, e, tb, _d=sys.excepthook):
    if issubclass(t, AssertionError):
        print('check failed:', e); sys.exit(1)
    _d(t, e, tb)
sys.excepthook = _fail
import subprocess
p = subprocess.run([sys.executable, '_tools/rag.py', 'pack', '--root', '_self', '--set', 'kb-sprint:plan'], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=300)
assert p.returncode == 0, ('rag.py pack --set kb-sprint:plan', p.returncode, p.stderr[-300:])
lines = [ln for ln in p.stdout.splitlines() if 'clause' in ln and 'every part' in ln]
assert lines, 'the kb-sprint:plan rule set holds no tested rule that a check mapped to a clause reads every part of that clause, the scratch or isolation parts included'
